The retrieved evidence shows mixed findings: some sources say well-designed educational television can improve literacy or language-related outcomes, especially for preschoolers and with adult support, while others say toddlers may show no language benefit from TV or DVDs [d2][d7][d4][d11].  
Several sources also indicate that co-viewing and interaction matter, and that person-to-person conversation remains more effective than screen exposure alone for language development [d1][d7][d10].  
So the best evidence-based answer is: children can sometimes learn certain language or literacy skills from educational television, but the results depend on age, program quality, and adult involvement, and television is not as effective as live social interaction [d2][d6][d10][d12].
